answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate churn pressure, but memory_73 and exp_73 show that promotional_pricing produces short-term signup lift (+31%) with severe long-term damage (-12% retention, poor renewal). This contradicts the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Instead, activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action without the retention penalty. Combined with signup simplification (memory_31, exp_31: +9% activation) and shortened onboarding (memory_86), this creates a stacked engagement strategy that increases perceived product value and time-to-value—the real competitive moat against price-based competition. Referral incentives (memory_57) work only for established customers, not useful for retention of price-sensitive churn risk. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment. A standard experiment with activation_messaging on at-risk SMB cohorts tests whether deepened early engagement can offset price sensitivity through value realization, avoiding the long-tail revenue destruction that discounting produces.
